Standard: The engine can independently ingest sheet ice and hailstones as described below without: a. Non-recoverable flameout or stall (per section 7.2.6). b. Violating engine operating limits. c. Impairment of any functional capability. d. Damage that requires corrective action prior to next maintenance opportunity. Sheet ice: a. 7 to 9 pieces of ice of varying size and shape. 5 lbs total weight of all ice pieces with no single piece weighing more than 0.75 lb. Ice size, shape, and thickness is informed by inlet ice accretion characteristics. b. Ingestion velocity simulates ice from inlet lip being sucked into the engine or 50 ft/s, whichever is more damaging. c. Ingestion occurs at the most damaging thrust or power setting at takeoff, cruise, and descent operating conditions. Hailstones: a. 30, 1-inch diameter hailstones, maximum of 10 at a time. b. Ingestion velocity is 750 ft/s, maximum cruise true airspeed up to 15000 ft, or maximum true airspeed for any defined low-level, high-speed mission, whichever is most damaging. c. Ingestion occurs at the most damaging power setting at takeoff, cruise, and descent operating condition, or at the defined power setting for low-level, high-speed mission. For inlet capture areas greater than 2100 in2 follow 14 CFR 33.77, Minimum Ice Slab Dimensions table for quantity, size, and associated weight of sheet ice, and 14 CFR 33.78, All Engines section for number and size of hailstones. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Analysis is conducted to determine the critical ingestion conditions affecting engine power loss, operability, and damage.
(2) Impact analysis is conducted for rotating and static hardware to assess strain, strain rate, deflection, deformation, and potential clashing or interaction with other components. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Full engine test in a ground-based sea level test cell is necessary. Test includes critical ingestion conditions determined by analysis (or component and rig test if relevant). For hail ingestion engine test, one-third to one-half of the hailstones should be aimed at the critical inlet face area with the remainder randomly distributed over the inlet face area. The hailstones should be ingested in a rapid sequence to simulate hailstorm encounter.
